blocks.text: Consider two bodies having masses m₁ and m₂, moving with velocities v⃗₁i and v⃗₂i along the same line such that v⃗₁i > v⃗₂i. In such a case m₁ is regarded as projectile and m₂ as target. After time t both the bodies make inelastic collision and stick together. Let their combined mass become m₁ + m₂ which moves with final velocity v⃗f after collision.

blocks.alt: Before collision: ball m1 with velocity v1i and a bigger ball m2 with velocity v2i, both to the right. After collision: one larger body m1 + m2 with a dark core, moving to the right with velocity vf.
blocks.caption: Figure 2.16: Perfectly inelastic collision in one dimension (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 2.16).

blocks.text: Since the collision is perfectly inelastic, the total momentum of balls is conserved. Using law of conservation of momentum.

blocks.latex: \text{Total momentum of system before collision} = \text{Total momentum of the system after collision}

This is the amount of kinetic energy lost during inelastic collision. From the forgoing analysis, it is clear that energy is lost during an inelastic collision in one dimension.

blocks.title: Example 2.10
blocks.problem: A projectile of mass 2 kg is moving with an initial velocity of 4 m s⁻¹ towards right and hits the target at rest of mass 3 kg, after collision the two masses stick together and move as single body with a velocity of 1.6 m s⁻¹. Show law of conservation of momentum and energy losses during perfect inelastic collision.
steps:
Initial momentum in x-direction
pₓ = m₁v₁ₓ + m₂v₂ₓ   As v₂ₓ = 0
= (2 kg × 4 m s⁻¹) + (3 kg × 0) = 8 kg m s⁻¹

As the combined mass is M = m₁ + m₂ = 2 kg + 3 kg = 5 kg
and the final velocity is vfx = 1.6 m s⁻¹

Final momentum is
M vfx = 5 kg × 1.6 m s⁻¹ = 8 kg m s⁻¹

Initial K.E. = ½m₁v₁i² + ½m₂v₂i²
= ½ × 2 kg × (4 m s⁻¹)² + ½ × 3 kg × 0
= 16 kg m² s⁻² + 0 = 16 J

Final K.E. = K.E final = ½(m₁ + m₂)vf²
= ½ × 5 kg × (1.6 m s⁻¹)² = 6.4 kg m² s⁻² = 6.4 J

Energy Loss = K.E initial - K.E final
= 16 J - 6.4 J = 9.6 J
blocks.answer: This is valid example of a perfectly inelastic collision in 2D, where the two bodies stick together after collision showing that momentum is conserved but kinetic energy is lost.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Both bodies move along the same straight line (the x-direction) before and after the collision, so this is a perfectly inelastic collision in one dimension, not in 2D.
